name: telegram
why: telegram is the one rail on the list that does not need a number at all, which is why it is second and why it is split in two. a bot is a token and a webhook; a user account is a person, and a person needs a number. the bot half belongs to the umbrella lane that already reads it, and the number half belongs here, because catching the signup code is the whole trick this package owns.
flow: decide which rail you actually want: a bot that answers in groups and channels, or an account that reads and talks as a user
the bot rail is a token from botfather and a webhook with a secret, and needs no number
the user rail needs a number, and the sms code goes to heyphony instead of a handset
whoever signs up holds the identity: a user account is a person, and telegram treats it as one

bot.what: a bot token, a webhook url and a secret header: no number, no phone, no sim
bot.why_preferred: it is the rail telegram actually supports for programs. no number to burn, no account to lose, revocable with one command, and the umbrella lane already reads it

steps.about: create the bot with botfather and keep the token he hands back
steps.cmd: open https://t.me/BotFather  # /newbot, name it, paste the token into TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
steps.note: the token is the credential, so it lives in the secret store, never in a readme or a shell history

steps.about: point telegram at the catcher, with a secret header the lane checks in constant time
confirm what telegram thinks the webhook is

user-account.what: a telegram account as a person, signed up on the did and read from a desktop session
user-account.why_risky: telegram asks more of a number than signal does, and a voip did is a number it has seen before. expect a chat, a wait, or a refusal, and never treat the account as replaceable: losing it loses the contacts

steps.about: install the desktop app on the machine that will hold the session
steps.cmd: apt install telegram-desktop  # or the flatpak, on a host with a display

steps.about: enter the did as the number; the code goes to heyphony, not to a handset
steps.note: telegram sends the code in-app if another session is already signed in, and by sms only otherwise

steps.about: type the code, and the two step password if the account has one

install.about: the bot rail needs nothing installed: it is https calls to telegram's own api
install.source: telegram bot api: getMe, setWebhook with secret_token, getWebhookInfo

verify.about: the token is real and names the bot it belongs to
a message from a whitelisted chat arrives in the lane, not just in a curl answer
verify.cmd: comms watch telegram  # or: bin/comms inbox --channel telegram

refused.user-api-id-as-a-bot: an mtproto api id is not a bot token: using one binds the account behind it to everything the client does
refused.bulk-broadcast: a bot that messages strangers is spam with a public api, and telegram blocks it faster than the carriers do
refused.group-scraping: reading every member of a group to find people to talk to is the same act as buying a list
refused.second-account-after-a-ban: a new number after a ban is the same person wearing a second face, which is not a workaround, it is a rerun

evidence: method names and the secret_token argument are telegram's own bot api; nothing has been created or linked here, and the user account path has not been attempted with a voip did
